This row occurs with mass13/32 in an explicit five-bit Boolean sign with pair-slice negative counts(6,1,2,1); all other rows provide margin (27-9log2(3))/32>0 and the whole pair satisfies the rate-two inequality. The real four-bit sign-amplitude function F(x,y)=2a_y(-1)^(x dot y)/sqrt(26) has every pair slice of unit L2 norm and uniform physical query marginals, yet fails the whole rate-two inequality; it is explicitly nonBoolean. An exact exhaustive certificate proves Omega>=-2(Inf_i+Inf_j) for all labelled Boolean tables n<=4 and every pair, without an all-dimensional extrapolation.
